Sincere seekers, self-knowledge, and historically natural nonbelievers provide reason to accept at least some nonculpable nonbelief.

bridges.statement: Evaluate divine presence and absence within the antecedent Christian story rather than abstract perfect-being theism alone.
Temporary hiddenness may serve development, prevent hardening or apostasy, enable testimony, and preserve a longer redemptive process.
Conscience, trust, responsiveness to the good, and relational seeking can connect people with God despite sparse explicit belief.
